reason: E1 shows a linear correlation between Cr content and tensile strength, but only from room-temperature MD simulations, not high-temperature wear. E2 demonstrates Cr2O3 formation and improved wear resistance for a different HEA (FeCoNiMnCu) on steel at 800 °C, but does not involve FeNiCrCoCu or Cr doping. The key premise that additional Cr yields a more continuous, adherent oxide in FeNiCrCoCu is not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Increasing Cr content in FeNiCrCoCu linearly increases tensile strength
Cr2O3 formation on HEA coatings at 800 °C enhances wear resistance
Additional Cr doping promotes a more continuous, adherent Cr2O3 layer
A denser Cr2O3 scale reduces oxidation spallation and direct metal contact during wear
